page: Amazon Web Services c8g.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the ARMv9 architecture using Neoverse-V2 cores, this instance features 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with no hyperthreading. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and includes a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with the stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Geekbench multi-core score both placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, reaching top-tier status in both cached read-only small block and uncached large block read/write tests. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang, perform in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores landing in the average category.

The instance offers high resource density and compute efficiency for multi-threaded workloads, though it presents a tradeoff for applications requiring high single-core speed or local NVMe storage. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the dedicated ARM64 core layout, which delivers strong multi-core scaling without the overhead of hyperthreading. This profile is highly suitable for multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-to-large LLM text generation.
